name: Philosophical-Question-Answering
description: A philosophical question answering dataset of 200 open-ended questions with free-form explanatory answers. It evaluates a model's ability to answer knowledge-intensive questions about philosophical concepts, arguments, and historical figures without a provided context passage.
card_text: This dataset contains 200 text-only philosophical question-answer pairs. Each sample consists of a single open-ended question in the input and a concise explanatory answer in the output. The questions cover topics such as analogical arguments, Islamic philosophy, and philosophical works. Answers are written in a factual, expository style and typically range from one to a few sentences. No supporting context, multiple-choice options, or dialogue history is provided, so the model must rely on its own philosophical knowledge to produce the answer.

question.semantics: A single open-ended philosophical question asking about a concept, argument, text, or philosopher. It is the sole input and directly prompts the model to produce a free-form answer.

answer.semantics: A concise, expository answer that names or explains philosophical concepts, works, or arguments in response to the question. It is generated without any supporting context passage.

meta.meta_structure_description: Each sample is a single-turn question-answer pair. The input object contains one open-ended philosophical question in input.question, and the output object contains a free-form explanatory answer in output.answer. There is no supporting context passage, multiple-choice options, dialogue history, or external evidence; the answer must be supplied from the model's philosophical knowledge.
